definitions.explanation: the ability to perceive things beyond the five physical senses

examples.japanese: {第|だい}{六感|ろっかん}で{危険|きけん}を{感|かん}じた。
examples.english: I sensed danger with my sixth sense.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{六感|ろっかん}が{鋭|するど}い。
examples.english: She has a sharp sixth sense.

examples.japanese: {六感|ろっかん}を{信|しん}じて{行動|こうどう}することにした。
examples.english: I decided to act on my intuition.

notes:
{六感|ろっかん} refers to perception beyond the five physical senses — intuition, gut feeling, or a mysterious ability to sense things.

FULL EXPRESSION:
More commonly said as {第|だい}{六感|ろっかん} (the sixth sense). Both forms are used.

THE FIVE SENSES ({五感|ごかん}):
- {視覚|しかく}: sight
- {聴覚|ちょうかく}: hearing
- {嗅覚|きゅうかく}: smell
- {味覚|みかく}: taste
- {触覚|しょっかく}: touch

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {第|だい}{六感|ろっかん}が{働|はたら}く: sixth sense kicks in
- {六感|ろっかん}が{鋭|するど}い: to have a sharp sixth sense
- {六感|ろっかん}を{信|しん}じる: to trust one's intuition

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {直感|ちょっかん}: intuition (more common in everyday speech)
- {勘|かん}: hunch, gut feeling (casual)
